gap.missing_evidence: No source establishes a transferable generic patience/abandonment hazard or distribution from observed individual waiting-state entry and departure times, with cohort, conditioning, censoring and competing-care outcomes. The cross-sectional LWBS risk study (Rathlev et al., Western Journal of Emergency Medicine, published 2020-08-25, DOI 10.5811/westjem.2020.6.47084; PMC7514399) defines LWBS after three unanswered calls 15 minutes apart but says exact departure time was usually unknown. Its hourly process measures and comparative cross-sectional outcome support risk associations, not a time-to-event hazard, patience distribution or departure-time observation. METEOR 621840 describes presentation-to-commencement-of-non-admitted-care elapsed minutes and explicitly excludes did-not-wait and advised-and-left episodes; the captured item is marked Superseded 2021-10-20 (Tasmanian Health registration separately Superseded 2023-03-22). It is historical definition/lead evidence only; current dataset metadata and mapping are unvalidated. Neither source establishes waiting entry, exact departure, censoring, or competing clinical-care endpoints for a current cohort. Unknown departure must remain unknown/censored, never a zero-duration event. Boarding is a distinct competing state/outcome and the sources do not resolve its observation or endpoint rules.
gap.owner: CareOps ED data owner, coordinated by the P1 evidence coordinator
gap.impact: Patience and abandonment remain unparameterized. Do not fit a hazard/distribution, infer individual waiting durations from aggregate LWBS proportions, or promote these sources into a generic or Cairns default. An empirical abandonment process cannot be calibrated or validated until the eligible waiting cohort, time origin, departure/event clock, censoring, competing clinical care/boarding, and missing endpoint rules are established.
